title: Dog-Trade Claims Need Records, Quarantine, and Abolition by 2030
excerpt: Claims about stolen pets, poison bait, and unquarantined transport require named records. Public-health risk still demands strict quarantine and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Claims of cyanide bait, stolen companions, and secret dog shipments cannot be presented as fact without police records, court judgments, seizure reports, or named health alerts. Those records are absent here. Silence cannot protect an illicit trade, but it cannot be filled with invented raids or victims either.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

“Farm-raised dogs” is not proof of lawful origin. Any defensible supply chain needs identifiable ownership, transport documents, veterinary inspection, quarantine compliance, and records that authorities can verify. Without those controls, buyers cannot distinguish farm origin from stolen family animals or animals moved outside inspection systems. The burden belongs to operators who profit from the trade.

Biosecurity starts before symptoms

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. See World Health Organization guidance.

Household exposure incidents and commercial transport failures are separate dimensions of biosecurity. Neither should be blurred into an unsupported causal story. Both demand transparent enforcement, veterinary quarantine, and public reporting.

Vietnamese communities can close legal gaps

Families, pet owners, veterinarians, and local reform leaders can demand records, inspections, and protection from theft. SDE’s campaign demand goes beyond any single health target: complete national abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
